description:
Assess host-side image-test and recovery residue from legacy REQ-0001 before cleanup. Read-only inventory of .codex/sdlc/recovery/REQ-0001-GOAL-COUNT-SYSTEM-RESETS/ (about 7.3 GiB allocated across four baseline-clone.img copies plus journals/baselines) and .codex/sdlc/req-0001-offset-test/ (about 1.9 GiB allocated, includes failed image_8.26.0 and saved baselines). Match exact source/copy/replay/marker identities and references from retained recovery journals and legacy plan. Record file ownership, sizes, hashes/metadata as authorized, active mounts/loops/processes, archive locations, retention rationale, and clone references. Two quarantine markers remain present and root-owned; contents were unreadable under current permissions, so unknown evidence must fail closed rather than imply safe deletion. etc/sdlc.conf still selects .codex/sdlc as active runtime/shared-lock root; never treat whole directory as obsolete. Deliver per-path KEEP, ARCHIVE, SAFE-CANDIDATE, or RECOVERY-REQUIRED classification and concrete later cleanup/recovery proposal with verification, rollback, access needs, and exact authority boundaries. Preserve original var/ image/kernel files, quarantine markers, failed copy, referenced clones, journals, baselines, active locks, and source hashes. This item performs no deletion, image mount/mutation, restoration, marker clearing, device access, or legacy-workflow resumption. Recovery or reclamation of protected residue needs separately approved procedure proving restoration under existing image-lock/quarantine rules. Actual reclaimable bytes remain unproven.

Migration-chain consumer contract: provide stable inventory/disposition evidence for ITM-0004 shared-safety dependency audit and ITM-0006 archival/readiness. Inspect host metadata and accessible retained evidence only; any image access remains subject to existing shared image-lock and quarantine rules. Root-owned unreadable entries stay UNKNOWN/RECOVERY-REQUIRED with explicit missing evidence and access needs; no successful complete-hash inventory or deletion claim. Completion requires honest coverage of candidate roots and precise retention boundaries, not recovery or release of quarantine. Any later required mutation/recovery remains separate approved scope. Final offline build must not consume failed image or these protected clones.

Latest artifact-ownership ruling: All these folders belong to the planning, implementation and QA stage and should be managed under .codex/sdlc as in Specz (with claude). ITM-0002 supplies tested durable artifact publication, recovery, and immutable review binding before this assessment. Publish inventory/disposition reports as managed per-item stage artifacts under .codex/sdlc, with immutable bundle locators for ITM-0004 and ITM-0006. The new artifact namespace is a protected managed sibling, not reclaimable image residue. Existing locks/quarantine/recovery/failed copies/clones/journals remain unchanged. All original read-only scope, unknown-evidence handling, retention and no-recovery boundaries remain intact.
